topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its intended learning outcomes regarding cancer treatments.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Their Limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities of cancer treatment—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with the challenges of systemic toxicity and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that selectively target the intrinsic molecular defects and signaling dependencies of cancer cells.

topics.label: Oncogene Targeting and Kinase Inhibitor Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapies directed against hyperactivated oncogenic driver kinases and the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Cancer Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the use of engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to selectively target cancer cell surface proteins.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Mobilization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system interacts with tumors and the therapeutic methods developed to harness and engineer T cells to destroy cancer cells.

topics.label: Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the overarching progress, clinical challenges, and future prospects of cancer treatment.
